lines.text: **[12.3 --- Acceptable Fallback Positions (Yellow)]{.underline}**
**Representation (a) --- No Prior Control Agreement:**

> **Fallback A --- Knowledge-Qualified Representation.** Accept a modified representation that the bank \"has no actual knowledge of\" any competing control agreement, rather than a flat representation that none exists. This formulation shifts the burden from a strict no-exceptions representation to a knowledge-qualified representation that accommodates the bank\'s concern about conducting a comprehensive internal search. However, it still provides Pinnacle with a contractual basis for a claim if a competing agreement surfaces and the bank had actual knowledge of it at the time of the ACA. Sample language:

> *\"To the Bank\'s actual knowledge, the Bank has not entered into any agreement with any other person pursuant to which the Bank has agreed to comply with instructions or entitlement orders concerning any Account originated by such other person.\"*

> **Fallback B --- Forward-Looking Covenant.** If the bank refuses even a knowledge-qualified representation, require the bank to agree as a covenant (rather than a representation) that it will not enter into any future control agreement or similar agreement with respect to the Accounts without the prior written consent of the Secured Party. This approach does not address the backward-looking question of whether a prior control agreement exists, but it prevents the bank from creating a competing interest going forward. Sample language:

> *\"The Bank agrees that it will not enter into any agreement with any other person pursuant to which the Bank agrees to comply with instructions or entitlement orders concerning any Account originated by such other person, without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.\"*

The preferred approach is to combine Fallback A and Fallback B: the bank makes a knowledge-qualified representation regarding the past and a forward-looking covenant regarding the future. This composite formulation provides reasonable protection in both directions.
**Representation (c) --- Account Renaming Notice:**

> Accept a reduction to fifteen (15) days\' notice (from thirty days), which is sufficient for Pinnacle to update its records and, if necessary, amend the ACA to reflect the new account number. Accept a carve-out for changes required by law or regulatory order, provided that the bank must notify the Secured Party promptly (within five (5) business days) after any such change. Do not accept ten days --- this is insufficient processing time, particularly if the ACA amendment requires signature by all three parties.
**[12.4 --- Walk-Away / Escalation Triggers (Red)]{.underline}**

> • Deletion of representation (a) (no prior control agreement) without any replacement covenant or knowledge-qualified representation --- **escalate to Diana Whitford**. This is a significant gap in the ACA\'s protective framework. A competing control agreement could give a third party priority over Pinnacle\'s security interest under UCC § 9-327. While Pinnacle can conduct its own due diligence (e.g., UCC searches) to identify competing liens, a UCC search will not reveal a competing control agreement because control agreements are not filed in the public record. The bank\'s representation is the only mechanism by which Pinnacle can obtain assurance that no competing control arrangement exists.

> • Deletion of representation (e) (bank status under UCC) --- generally not a serious concern if the bank is a nationally chartered bank (as Ironbridge is under OCC Charter No. 18742), because a national bank clearly satisfies the UCC\'s definition of a \"bank.\" However, if the depository institution\'s status is unclear --- for example, if it is a non-bank financial institution, a credit union, or an entity organized under the laws of a foreign jurisdiction --- flag for review by Thomas Orr to confirm that the institution qualifies as a \"bank\" under UCC § 9-102(a)(8) and that the ACA will confer valid \"control\" over a \"deposit account.\"
**[SECTION 13 --- FEE ARRANGEMENTS]{.underline}**
**[13.1 --- Overview]{.underline}**

Banks customarily charge annual maintenance fees for administering ACAs and frequently seek reimbursement of their outside counsel\'s legal fees incurred in reviewing and negotiating the ACA. These are commercial terms, not structural UCC issues; they do not affect perfection, control, or the priority of Pinnacle\'s security interest. Accordingly, the deal team has broader latitude to negotiate these provisions without the structural constraints that apply to the substantive provisions addressed in Sections 2 through 12 above.

However, fee provisions must be reviewed carefully to ensure that they do not contain structural hooks --- for example, a provision that makes the bank\'s obligations under the ACA (including compliance with a NOEC) conditional on the Depositor\'s payment of fees. Such a provision would convert a commercial term into a structural issue with potentially devastating consequences for Pinnacle\'s control rights.
**[13.2 --- Annual Maintenance Fees]{.underline}**

Annual maintenance fees for ACAs are standard in the banking industry and are generally borne by the Depositor (not the Secured Party) as an operating cost of maintaining the banking relationship. The current market range for ACA annual maintenance fees is approximately \$1,500 to \$5,000 per account per year, depending on the bank, the size and complexity of the account, and the geographic market.

In the current Ironbridge matter, the bank has proposed a standard fee of \$3,500 per account per year. With three controlled accounts (●●●●-4471, ●●●●-4472, and ●●●●-4473), the total annual maintenance fee burden is \$10,500 per year. This is within the market range and is acceptable without further negotiation.

No escalation is required for annual maintenance fees within the \$1,500 to \$5,000 per account per year range. If the bank proposes annual fees exceeding \$5,000 per account per year, flag for Diana Whitford\'s awareness, but note that this is a cost issue rather than a structural issue and is unlikely to affect the overall ACA negotiation.
**[13.3 --- Legal-Fee Reimbursement]{.underline}**

Banks increasingly request one-time reimbursement of their outside counsel\'s legal fees incurred in reviewing and negotiating the ACA. This practice has become more common over the past several years as ACA negotiations have become more protracted and bank counsel has become more actively involved in the process. Legal-fee reimbursement provisions are typically structured as a one-time payment due upon execution of the ACA.

In the current Ironbridge matter, the bank has inserted a \$15,000 one-time legal-fee reimbursement provision (Section 12 of the bank\'s Turn 1 markup). The bank\'s outside counsel is Blackmere Fox LLP.

**Client Directive:** Annual maintenance fees are acceptable as a customary cost of the deposit account relationship. Legal-fee reimbursement, however, should be negotiated down or capped to ensure that the cost is proportionate to the scope of the engagement. The following fallback positions are pre-authorized:

> **Fallback A --- 50% Reduction.** Cap legal-fee reimbursement at \$7,500 (50% of the bank\'s requested amount). Present this as Pinnacle\'s initial counter-position, noting that \$7,500 is a reasonable fee for a straightforward ACA review and negotiation. Emphasize that Pinnacle\'s form ACA is based on market-standard provisions and that the scope of the bank\'s counsel\'s work should be limited to reviewing and commenting on Pinnacle\'s form, not drafting a new agreement from scratch.

> **Fallback B --- Intermediate Cap with Documentation.** Accept \$10,000 as the maximum reimbursement and require the bank to provide supporting documentation (invoices or fee statements) before payment. This fallback is appropriate if the bank rejects the \$7,500 cap and pushes for a higher amount.

> **Fallback C --- Full Amount as Closing Concession.** Accept the full \$15,000 if it is the last open commercial issue and resolving it would close the ACA negotiation. In this case, ensure that the provision specifies that the \$15,000 is a one-time fee and that no additional legal-fee reimbursement will be required for future amendments, modifications, or supplements to the ACA. This cap on future fees is important because ACA amendments (e.g., to add or remove accounts, to update notice provisions, or to reflect successor-bank events) are relatively common over the life of a credit facility and could generate additional legal-fee reimbursement obligations if not capped.
**[13.4 --- Walk-Away / Escalation Triggers (Red)]{.underline}**

> • Any provision requiring Pinnacle (rather than the Depositor) to pay the bank\'s annual maintenance fees or legal-fee reimbursement --- **escalate**. These are customarily Depositor obligations. If the bank insists that the Secured Party be jointly liable for fees, the provision should specify that the Depositor has primary responsibility and that the Secured Party\'s liability is limited to circumstances where the Depositor fails to pay.

> • Any fee provision that makes the bank\'s obligations under the ACA (including compliance with a NOEC) conditional on the payment of fees --- **hard stop**. The bank\'s performance of its obligations under the ACA --- and in particular its obligation to comply with Pinnacle\'s instructions upon delivery of a NOEC --- cannot be conditioned on fee payment. A provision that permits the bank to refuse to comply with a NOEC because the Depositor has not paid its annual maintenance fee would effectively allow a fee dispute to defeat Pinnacle\'s control over its collateral. This is structurally unacceptable and must be rejected without exception.

The ACA is a tripartite agreement to which the Depositor is a signatory. In most transactions, the Depositor is represented by its own counsel, who may have separate comments on the ACA\'s provisions --- particularly those that impose obligations on the Depositor (e.g., indemnification, replacement-account covenants, fee obligations) or that restrict the Depositor\'s access to its own accounts.

The negotiator should maintain open communication with the Depositor\'s counsel regarding the status of the ACA negotiation. In the current Graycliff matter, the Depositor\'s counsel is Catherine Voss at Dunlevy Rourke LLP. The negotiator should not negotiate the ACA bilaterally with bank counsel without keeping Depositor\'s counsel informed. from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.enum.style import WD_STYLE_TYPE
from docx.enum.text import WD_LINE_SPACING
from docx.enum.section import WD_ORIENT
from datetime import datetime
import os

OUT = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'output')
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

BLUE = '0000FF'
RED = 'C00000'
GRAY = '666666'
NAVY = '17365D'
LIGHT_BLUE = 'D9EAF7'
LIGHT_GRAY = 'F2F2F2'


def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd')
        tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)


def set_cell_margins(cell, top=80, start=100, bottom=80, end=100):
    tc = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcMar = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if tcMar is None:
        tcMar = OxmlElement('w:tcMar')
        tcPr.append(tcMar)
    for m, v in [('top', top), ('start', start), ('bottom', bottom), ('end', end)]:
        node = tcMar.find(qn(f'w:{m}'))
        if node is None:
            node = OxmlElement(f'w:{m}')
            tcMar.append(node)
        node.set(qn('w:w'), str(v))
        node.set(qn('w:type'), 'dxa')


def set_repeat_table_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    tblHeader = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader')
    tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'), 'true')
    trPr.append(tblHeader)


def set_cell_width(cell, width_inches):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcW = tcPr.find(qn('w:tcW'))
    if tcW is None:
        tcW = OxmlElement('w:tcW')

    doc = Document()
    sec = doc.sections[0]
    sec.top_margin = Inches(0.65)
    sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.65)
    sec.left_margin = Inches(0.75)
    sec.right_margin = Inches(0.75)
    styles = doc.styles
    normal = styles['Normal']
    normal.font.name = 'Arial'
    normal.font.size = Pt(9.5)
    normal.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    normal.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.05
    for sname, size, color in [('Title', 18, NAVY), ('Heading 1', 13, NAVY), ('Heading 2', 10.5, NAVY), ('Heading 3', 9.5, NAVY)]:
        st = styles[sname]
        st.font.name = 'Arial'
        st.font.size = Pt(size)
        st.font.bold = True
        st.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)
        st.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(9 if sname != 'Title' else 0)
        st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    if 'Small' not in styles:
        st = styles.add_style('Small', WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH)
    else:
        st = styles['Small']
    st.font.name = 'Arial'; st.font.size = Pt(8); st.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    if 'CaptionGray' not in styles:
        st = styles.add_style('CaptionGray', WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH)
    else:
        st = styles['CaptionGray']
    st.font.name = 'Arial'; st.font.size = Pt(8.5); st.font.italic = True; st.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    header = sec.header.paragraphs[0]
    header.text = short
    header.style = 'Small'
    header.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
    footer = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
    footer.style = 'Small'
    add_page_number(footer)

    settings = doc.settings.element
    track = settings.find(qn('w:trackRevisions'))
    if track is None:
        settings.append(OxmlElement('w:trackRevisions'))
    core = doc.core_properties
    core.title = title
    core.author = 'Hargrave Stein & Collier LLP'
    core.subject = 'Ironbridge / Graycliff / Pinnacle Account Control Agreement'
    core.comments = 'Second-turn redline prepared against Ironbridge Bank Turn 1 markup dated May 5, 2025.'
    return doc


def set_run_font(run, color=None, bold=None, italic=None, underline=None, strike=None, size=None):
    run.font.name = 'Arial'
    if size: run.font.size = Pt(size)
    if color: run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)
    if bold is not None: run.bold = bold
    if italic is not None: run.italic = italic
    if underline is not None: run.underline = underline
    if strike is not None: run.font.strike = strike


def add_plain(p, text, **kwargs):
    r = p.add_run(text)
    set_run_font(r, **kwargs)
    return r

_rev_id = 1

def add_revision(p, text, kind='ins', author='Pinnacle / Hargrave Stein'):
    global _rev_id
    wrapper = OxmlElement('w:ins' if kind == 'ins' else 'w:del')
    wrapper.set(qn('w:id'), str(_rev_id)); _rev_id += 1
    wrapper.set(qn('w:author'), author)
    wrapper.set(qn('w:date'), '2025-05-09T12:00:00Z')
    r = OxmlElement('w:r')
    rPr = OxmlElement('w:rPr')
    color = OxmlElement('w:color'); color.set(qn('w:val'), BLUE if kind == 'ins' else RED); rPr.append(color)
    if kind == 'ins':
        u = OxmlElement('w:u'); u.set(qn('w:val'), 'single'); rPr.append(u)
    else:
        st = OxmlElement('w:strike'); st.set(qn('w:val'), 'true'); rPr.append(st)
    r.append(rPr)
    t = OxmlElement('w:delText' if kind == 'del' else 'w:t')

    return wrapper


def add_label(p, text):
    r = p.add_run(text)
    set_run_font(r, color=NAVY, bold=True)
    return r


def add_clause(doc, heading, parts, style='Normal'):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style)
    if heading:
        add_label(p, heading)
    for part in parts:
        if isinstance(part, tuple): add_revision(p, part[1], part[0])
        else: add_plain(p, part)
    return p


def add_section_heading(doc, text):
    return doc.add_paragraph(text, style='Heading 1')


def add_subheading(doc, text):
    return doc.add_paragraph(text, style='Heading 2')


def add_bullets(doc, items, level=0):
    for item in items:
        p = doc.add_paragraph(style='Normal')
        p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.25 + 0.2*level)
        p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.15)
        add_plain(p, '• ', color=NAVY, bold=True)

# DEPOSIT ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
This DEPOSIT ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is entered into as of \[DATE\], 2025 (the "Effective Date"), by and among:
**SECURED PARTY:** Pinnacle Capital Partners, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, and its successors and assigns (the "Secured Party");
**DEPOSITOR / DEBTOR:** Graycliff Industries, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Depositor" or "Debtor"); and
**DEPOSITORY BANK:** Ironbridge National Bank, N.A., a national banking association (the "Bank").
The Secured Party, the Depositor, and the Bank are each a "Party" and collectively the "Parties."
## RECITALS
WHEREAS, Depositor maintains the deposit accounts identified on Schedule A (collectively, the "Accounts" and each an "Account");

WHEREAS, Secured Party has been granted a security interest in the Accounts and funds credited thereto under the Credit Agreement dated April 14, 2025, maturing April 14, 2030, and related Loan Documents; and
WHEREAS, the Parties desire to establish "control" by Secured Party over the Accounts for purposes of perfection under the UCC.
NOW, THEREFORE, the Parties agree as follows:
# 1. DEFINITIONS
Capitalized terms not otherwise defined have the meanings assigned in the Loan Documents or, if not defined there, in the UCC.

**"Account" or "Deposit Account" means** each deposit account identified on Schedule A, including renewals, replacements, reclassifications, redesignations, or successor accounts, and all funds and proceeds credited thereto.

**"Business Day" means** any day on which Bank is open for substantially all commercial banking business at its offices in Charlotte, North Carolina, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal banking holidays.

**"Entitlement Order" means** [the term defined in UCC Section 8-102(a)(8), including any notification communicated to Bank directing the transfer, redemption, liquidation, or other disposition of a financial asset or interest therein, including any direction originated by Secured Party under this Agreement.]{.underline}

**"Event of Default" means** an "Event of Default" as defined in and determined under the Loan Documents. Bank has no duty to determine independently whether an Event of Default has occurred or is continuing.

**"Notice of Exclusive Control" or "NOEC" means** a written notice delivered by Secured Party to Bank in accordance with the Notices provision, directing Bank to comply exclusively with Secured Party's Instructions and to cease complying with Depositor's Instructions.

**"Instructions" means** any order, direction, instruction, request, or authorization regarding the disposition of funds in, or action to be taken or omitted with respect to, an Account, including wires, ACH transactions, checks, withdrawals, transfers, account closings, and account information.
**"UCC" means** the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of New York, except that mandatory UCC choice-of-law rules govern perfection and priority where applicable.
# 2. THE ACCOUNTS; ESTABLISHMENT OF CONTROL

2.1 Confirmation of Accounts. Bank confirms that each Account listed on Schedule A is maintained at Bank, is held in Depositor's name, and constitutes a "deposit account" within the meaning of the UCC.

**2.2 Establishment of Control.** Bank hereby agrees that, from and after the Effective Date, it will comply with [Entitlement Orders originated by Secured Party with respect to the Accounts and Instructions originated by Secured Party directing disposition of funds in the Accounts]{.underline} without further consent of Depositor, thereby establishing control by Secured Party within the meaning of UCC Sections 9-104(a)(2) and 8-106 to the extent applicable. This obligation is unconditional and is not subject to any condition other than delivery in accordance with the Notices provision.

2.3 No Changes to Accounts Without Consent. Bank shall not, without the prior written consent of Secured Party, change, close, redesignate, merge, combine, or consolidate an Account, or permit a change to authorized signatories that Secured Party has objected to in writing.

**2.4 Depositor's Consent.** Depositor irrevocably authorizes and consents to Bank's compliance with all [Instructions and Entitlement Orders]{.underline} originated by Secured Party without further consent or notice to Depositor.

**2.5 Depositor's Operating Rights Prior to NOEC.** [Prior to Bank's receipt of a NOEC, Depositor may operate the Accounts in the ordinary course of business, including customary debits, credits, transfers, ACH transactions, checks, and payroll payments, without prior consent of Secured Party. Upon Bank's receipt of a NOEC, Depositor's authority and access to issue Instructions with respect to the Accounts shall cease immediately and without qualification; Bank shall not accept or process any new Depositor Instruction. Bank may honor only an Instruction that was originated by Depositor and accepted by Bank before Bank's receipt of the NOEC and that is irrevocably in process, solely to the extent necessary to settle that item. Thereafter, Bank shall comply exclusively with Secured Party's Instructions and shall not require further consent of Depositor.]{.underline}
# 3. EXCLUSIVE CONTROL; CONFLICTING INSTRUCTIONS

**3.1 Effect of NOEC.** [Upon receipt of a NOEC, Bank shall immediately cease complying with Depositor's Instructions and shall comply solely and exclusively with Secured Party's Instructions and Entitlement Orders with respect to the Accounts. Bank shall freeze and block new automated or preauthorized debits and shall provide Secured Party with current account balances and transaction histories promptly upon request.]{.underline}

**3.2 No Requirement of Proof.** Bank shall not require evidence of an Event of Default, a court order, a judgment, a certificate from Depositor, or other documentation as a condition to compliance with a NOEC. Bank's sole obligation is to verify that the notice is written, purports to come from Secured Party or its authorized representative, is directed to Bank in accordance with the Notices provision, and requests exclusive compliance.

**3.3 Conflicting Instructions.** [In the event of a conflict between Instructions received from Secured Party and Instructions received from Depositor, the Instructions of Secured Party shall control and prevail at all times. Bank shall comply with Secured Party's Instructions immediately and shall comply with Depositor's Instructions only to the extent they are not inconsistent with Secured Party's Instructions and no NOEC is in effect.]{.underline}

**3.4 Notice and Rescission.** Bank shall promptly notify Secured Party of any conflicting Depositor Instruction. A NOEC remains in effect until Secured Party delivers a written rescission; following rescission, Depositor's ordinary-course rights under Section 2.5 resume.
# 4. NOEC COMPLIANCE PERIOD

**4.1 Compliance. Bank shall comply with a NOEC within** [three (3)]{.underline} Business Days following Bank's receipt and authentication of the NOEC. During that period, Bank shall use commercially reasonable efforts to implement the NOEC as promptly as practicable and shall not permit new Depositor debits, withdrawals, or transfers after receipt of the NOEC.

4.2 Existing Items. Bank shall not be liable for checks, ACH entries, or wire transfers irrevocably initiated and accepted before receipt of the NOEC that settle after the compliance period, provided Bank acts in good faith and uses commercially reasonable efforts to prevent further Depositor activity.
# 5. SUBORDINATION OF BANK LIENS; LIMITED SET-OFF

**5.1 Subordination.** [Bank hereby subordinates all Liens, security interests, encumbrances, claims, counterclaims, and rights of set-off that Bank may have in or with respect to the Accounts and the funds therein to the security interest of Secured Party, subject only to the limited rights expressly preserved in Section 5.2 and the 180-day lookback in Section 5.3.]{.underline}

**5.2 Limited Set-Off Scope.** [Notwithstanding the foregoing, Bank may exercise set-off or debit an Account only for a direct, matured, and liquidated obligation of Depositor to Bank arising under the deposit account agreements applicable to the Accounts, including customary documented account-maintenance, service, and transaction fees and chargebacks of returned or reversed items. No set-off or debit may be taken for a contingent, unmatured, unliquidated, disputed, derivative, loan, credit-facility, letter-of-credit, foreign-exchange, swap, or other obligation unrelated to the Accounts, or for any obligation owed to an affiliate of Bank. Any permitted debit remains subject to Secured Party's priority under Section 3 and shall not be used to defeat the effect of a NOEC.]{.underline}

**5.3 Lookback.** [one hundred eighty (180)]{.underline} days immediately preceding the date of delivery of a NOEC shall constitute the Lookback Period for any permitted Bank Lien, fee, charge, or returned item. Bank's Liens and set-off rights with respect to obligations arising before the Lookback Period are subordinated under this Agreement, and no permitted debit may be made after delivery of a NOEC except as expressly permitted by Section 5.2 and subject to Section 3.
5.4 Fees and return items must be documented and reported to Secured Party promptly upon request. Bank's rights under this Section do not condition or delay Bank's obligation to comply with a NOEC.
# 6. INDEMNIFICATION

6.1 Secured Party Indemnification. Secured Party agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Bank and its officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives from Losses arising out of Bank's good-faith compliance with Secured Party's Instructions, Entitlement Orders, or a NOEC, or action taken in good-faith reliance on this Agreement.

**6.2 Scope of Indemnification.** [The indemnification obligations shall not extend to Losses to the extent determined by a court of competent jurisdiction in a final, non-appealable judgment to have resulted from the Bank's gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or material breach of this Agreement.]{.underline}

6.3 Depositor Indemnification. Depositor shall indemnify Bank for Losses arising from Depositor's breach of this Agreement or third-party claims relating to the Accounts, except to the extent caused by the acts or omissions of Bank or Secured Party.
# 7. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
**7.1 Aggregate Liability Cap.** [No aggregate dollar cap shall apply to Bank's liability under or in connection with this Agreement.]{.underline}

7.2 Mutual Waiver of Consequential, Punitive, and Indirect Damages. NO PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO ANY OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE, OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES ARISING OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT, WHETHER BASED ON CONTRACT, TORT, STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER THEORY, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES; provided that this Section shall not limit any Party's obligations under the indemnification provisions or limit recovery of direct damages, including funds released in breach of this Agreement.
Pinnacle accepts the mutual waiver in Section 7.2 for purposes of this turn, subject to the reservation described in the cover note.
# 8. TERMINATION

8.1 Termination by Secured Party. This Agreement may be terminated upon the prior written consent of Secured Party after indefeasible payment in full of the Secured Obligations and release of the related security interests.

**8.2 Bank Termination.** [Bank may terminate this Agreement upon not less than ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Secured Party and Depositor; provided that during the notice period Bank shall continue to perform all obligations hereunder, including compliance with any outstanding NOEC, Depositor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish replacement accounts at a depository bank reasonably acceptable to Secured Party, and this Agreement shall not terminate until Secured Party has confirmed in writing that a replacement account control agreement has been executed and delivered. Secured Party may transition the Accounts to a replacement depository bank during the notice period, and Bank shall reasonably cooperate with that transition.]{.underline}
8.3 No unilateral termination by Depositor. Depositor may not terminate this Agreement without the prior written consent of Secured Party.
# 9. GOVERNING LAW; JURISDICTION

**9.1 Governing Law.** [This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and interpreted in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles that would require application of another jurisdiction's law. Matters relating to perfection, priority, and enforcement of security interests in the Accounts shall be determined under the UCC as in effect in the applicable jurisdiction under UCC Section 9-304.]{.underline}

9.2 Jurisdiction. Each Party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the federal and state courts located in New York County, New York, for actions arising out of or relating to this Agreement and consents to service of process as permitted by applicable law. The Parties waive trial by jury to the fullest extent permitted by law.
# 10. NOTICES

Notices, including a NOEC, may be delivered by hand, nationally recognized overnight courier, registered or certified mail, or confirmed electronic mail to the addresses designated by the Parties. A NOEC may be delivered by electronic mail to the Bank contact specified below, with confirmation of transmission. Notices are effective upon receipt or, for courier and mail, as provided in the Bank Turn 1 notice provision.

Bank: Ironbridge National Bank, N.A., Institutional Deposit Services, 401 South Tryon Street, 15th Floor, Charlotte, NC 28202; Attention: Jonathan Kehoe, Director --- Institutional Deposit Services.
# 11. FEES AND EXPENSES

11.1 Annual Maintenance Fee. Depositor shall pay Bank an annual ACA maintenance fee of \$3,500 per Account per annum, currently \$10,500 for the three Accounts. This annual fee is accepted without change.

**11.2 Legal-Fee Reimbursement.** [Depositor shall reimburse Bank for its documented outside legal fees incurred in connection with the review, negotiation, and execution of this Agreement, in an amount not to exceed \$7,500 or the actual documented fees incurred, whichever is less, payable once upon execution. No fee under this Section shall condition, delay, or limit Bank's obligations under this Agreement, including compliance with a NOEC.]{.underline}

**11.3 Priority of Fees.** [Fees and reimbursements payable under this Section remain subject to Sections 3 and 5 and shall not expand Bank's set-off or lien rights or condition Bank's performance of this Agreement.]{.underline}
# 12. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

**12.2 No Prior Control Agreements or Liens.** [To Bank's actual knowledge, Bank has not entered into any other control, blocked-account, escrow, or similar agreement pursuant to which Bank has agreed to comply with instructions or entitlement orders concerning any Account originated by another person, and Bank has received no notice of any Lien, claim, or adverse interest in the Accounts other than the interest of Secured Party contemplated by this Agreement. Bank will not enter into any competing control agreement concerning an Account without the prior written consent of Secured Party.]{.underline}

31: # Pinnacle's Responses
32: 
33: ## 1. Entitlement-order terminology (§ 2(a)) --- restore.
34: 
35: We cannot accept replacing "entitlement order" throughout the control provision with "instruction." The Pinnacle form intentionally uses the Article 8 term, together with Article 9 instruction language, to preserve the agreement's operation across the applicable UCC control frameworks. The redline restores "entitlement order" as defined in UCC § 8-102(a)(8) while retaining the Article 9 control language. This is necessary to avoid ambiguity regarding the UCC basis for control and perfection.
36: 
37: ## 2. Springing exclusive control / operating carve-out --- accept in concept; tighten.
38: 
39: Pinnacle accepts that Graycliff should continue ordinary-course operations before delivery of a Notice of Exclusive Control (NOEC). The Bank's Turn 1 wording is revised, however, to make the two phases explicit: pre-NOEC ordinary-course operation is permitted; upon receipt of an NOEC, Graycliff's authority and access to issue instructions cease immediately, the Bank may not accept new Depositor instructions, and the Bank must comply exclusively with Pinnacle's instructions. Only items already originated and accepted and irrevocably in process before receipt may settle.
40: 
41: ## 3. Conflicting-instructions waterfall (§ 3) --- reject Bank priority; restore Secured Party priority.
42: 
43: Pinnacle cannot accept a waterfall under which the Bank's set-off rights take priority over Secured Party instructions. The control agreement must provide a clear, contractual priority rule under which Pinnacle's instructions prevail. That structure is central to the UCC control arrangement and avoids leaving priority to the Bank's unilateral determination at the time of a conflict.
44: 
45: ## 4. Set-off scope (§ 4) --- counter-propose a narrow accommodation.
46: 
47: As a good-faith accommodation, Pinnacle has narrowed the Bank's set-off carve-out to direct, matured, liquidated obligations arising under the deposit account agreements themselves, including customary documented account fees and returned-item chargebacks. The redline excludes contingent, unmatured, unliquidated, disputed, derivative, loan, credit-facility, letter-of-credit, foreign-exchange, swap, and affiliate obligations. Any permitted debit remains subject to Pinnacle's priority and may not be used to defeat the effect of an NOEC.
48: 
49: ## 5. NOEC compliance period (§ 5) --- counter at three Business Days.
50: 
51: Five Business Days is too long in a default scenario involving approximately \$38.15 million of controlled deposits. Pinnacle's counter at three Business Days gives Ironbridge additional operational time beyond the two-day form period while preserving a prompt transition to exclusive control. This is a reasonable middle ground for the Bank's processing and authentication procedures.
52: 
53: ## 6. Indemnification / gross negligence (§ 6) --- reject; restore carve-out.
54: 
55: Pinnacle will not indemnify Ironbridge for Losses to the extent caused by the Bank's own gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or material breach. Extending indemnification to the Bank's gross negligence is inconsistent with standard market practice for account control agreements and would shift to Pinnacle the risk of the Bank's own serious misconduct.
56: 
57: ## 7. Aggregate liability cap (§ 7(a)) --- delete the \$50,000 cap.
58: 
59: The proposed \$50,000 aggregate cap is not acceptable. The three controlled accounts have aggregate balances of approximately \$38.15 million (\$22.35 million Operating, \$4.18 million Payroll, and \$11.62 million Collections). A \$50,000 cap is de minimis in relation to the assets subject to the control arrangement and would provide no meaningful accountability for a breach affecting those funds. The redline deletes the cap entirely.
60: 
61: ## 8. Consequential-damages waiver (§ 7(b)) --- leave in place for this turn, subject to reservation.
62: 
63: Pinnacle is prepared to leave the Bank's mutual waiver of consequential, punitive, and indirect damages in place for purposes of this turn, given that it is mutual and does not limit direct damages or the indemnification provisions. We reserve the right to revisit this provision if the liability-cap or related risk-allocation package changes materially.
64: 
65: ## 9. Lien subordination / lookback (§ 8) --- counter at 180 days.
66: 
67: The 90-day lookback is too short and would leave an unacceptable gap in the subordination protection for obligations arising before that period. Pinnacle's counter provides a 180-day lookback, which is the minimum period acceptable to Pinnacle, while preserving the Bank's ability to address obligations that materially predate the lookback.
68: 
69: ## 10. Termination (§ 9) --- reject 30-day unilateral termination; counter at 90 days with transition rights.
70: 
71: Pinnacle cannot accept a 30-day unilateral termination right with no replacement mechanism. Abrupt termination could impair perfection because the ACA is the operative control arrangement for the Accounts. As a practical compromise, the redline permits termination on at least 90 days' prior written notice, requires the Bank to continue performing during the notice period (including any outstanding NOEC), and gives Pinnacle an express right to transition the Accounts to a replacement depository bank before termination becomes effective.
72: 
73: ## 11. Governing law (§ 10) --- restore New York.
74: 
75: Pinnacle's position is firm that the Agreement should be governed by New York law. New York law is consistent with the Credit Agreement and related Loan Documents and provides a well-developed body of UCC Article 8 and Article 9 authority relevant to control and priority questions. The UCC § 9-304 choice-of-law rules continue to govern perfection and priority where mandatory.
76: 
77: ## 12. No prior control agreements / liens (§ 12) --- reinstate.
78: 
79: The redline restores the confirmations needed to support Pinnacle's first-priority control analysis: a knowledge-qualified Bank representation that it has not entered into a competing control arrangement and has received no notice of an adverse lien or claim, together with a Depositor representation that no prior control agreement or lien affects the Accounts. A UCC search will not disclose an unfiled control agreement, so this contractual confirmation is important to the perfection analysis.
80: 
81: ## 13. Successor-bank notification (§ 13) --- reinstate with 30-day notice.
82: 
83: The redline restores an obligation to provide at least 30 days' prior written notice of any merger, consolidation, assignment, transfer, or other successor-bank event affecting the Accounts. It also requires reasonable cooperation to maintain uninterrupted control, including a replacement account control agreement if reasonably requested. This notice is necessary to preserve the integrity and continuity of the control arrangement.
84: 
85: ## Fees (§ 11) --- accept annual fees; reduce legal-fee reimbursement.
86: 
87: Pinnacle accepts the proposed annual maintenance fee of \$3,500 per Account (\$10,500 total for the three Accounts). For the one-time legal-fee reimbursement, Pinnacle proposes a cap of \$7,500 or actual documented outside legal fees, whichever is less. The proposed amount is proportionate to a review of a market-standard ACA and demonstrates flexibility on a commercial, non-structural item. Fees may not condition or delay the Bank's control obligations, including compliance with an NOEC.
88: 
89: # Next Steps

This is a reasonable middle ground for the Bank's processing and authentication procedures.
## 6. Indemnification / gross negligence (§ 6) --- reject; restore carve-out.

Pinnacle will not indemnify Ironbridge for Losses to the extent caused by the Bank's own gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or material breach. Extending indemnification to the Bank's gross negligence is inconsistent with standard market practice for account control agreements and would shift to Pinnacle the risk of the Bank's own serious misconduct.
## 7. Aggregate liability cap (§ 7(a)) --- delete the \$50,000 cap.

The proposed \$50,000 aggregate cap is not acceptable. ## 8. Consequential-damages waiver (§ 7(b)) --- leave in place for this turn, subject to reservation.

No permitted debit may be made after delivery of a NOEC except as expressly permitted by Section 5.2 and subject to Section 3.
